speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have increasing pain and swelling in your right knee, and a history of a similar issue with your left ankle. To better understand your condition, could you describe the specific type of pain and when these episodes typically occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (Reiter's Syndrome). The clinical presentation of asymmetric oligoarthritis (knee and ankle), dysuria, and risk factors for sexually transmitted infections (young male, multiple partners, inconsistent condom use) is highly suggestive. Given the joint involvement and duration, I am requesting a Urinalysis and Urine Culture to confirm the presence of infection and potential urinary tract pathology.
